identity.title: Self-Supervised Denoising-Enhanced Dual-Site CRISPR Cascade Nanosphere Enables Amplification-Free Pathogen Detection.

content.abstract: Foodborne pathogens pose a major threat to global public health, necessitating rapid, sensitive, and deployable detection methods. Despite their considerable promise, current CRISPR-based diagnostics remain constrained by mandatory preamplification steps and insufficient sensitivity, hindering point-of-care application. Here, we introduce a self-supervised denoising-enhanced dual-site CRISPR cascade nanosphere (SD-DCCN) biosensing platform for on-site detection. The SD-DCCN integrates a CRISPR cascade architecture that reactivates the dormant catalytic potential of Cas12a by employing a universal split crRNA motif with two full-length crRNAs to synergistically boost the trans-cleavage activity, coupled with a self-supervised denoising algorithm on a visualized nanosphere platform that converts the amplified signal into a high-contrast quantitative readout. Our strategy eliminates the need for preamplification and achieves detection of Salmonella Typhimurium with a limit of detection as low as 16 CFU/mL, representing a 62.5-fold improvement over conventional amplification-free CRISPR assays. In addition, by integrating smartphone-readable tube analysis with qPCR-comparable sensitivity, the portable SD-DCCN presents a practical approach for rapid and on-site food safety monitoring. Furthermore, we quantify viable bacteria in diverse real food samples and validate the detection results against qPCR benchmarks. This platform holds great promise for CRISPR diagnosis of foodborne diseases, especially in resource-limited settings.
